ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the radius of the circle $ \odot O$ is 2 cm, and a regular hexagon is inscribed in $ \odot O$. What is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect BO, CO, and OA.\\
From the given information, both $\triangle OBC$ and $\triangle AOB$ are equilateral triangles,\\
$\therefore \angle AOB = \angle OBC = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OA \parallel BC$,\\
$\therefore$ The area of $\triangle OBC$ is equal to the area of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ The area of the shaded region is equal to the area of the sector OBC $= \frac{60^\circ \pi \times 2^2}{360^\circ} = \boxed{\frac{2\pi}{3}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle with O as the center, and a regular hexagon is inscribed in the circle, with vertices labeled in order as A, B, C, D, E, F. The shaded part is located at the lower left of the circle, enclosed by side AB, diagonal AC, and the lower small arc corresponding to BC; the center O is inside the hexagon. Reasoning: Connect OB, OC, OA. A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle, so the central angle corresponding to adjacent vertices is 60°, and the side length equals the radius, so triangle OBC and triangle AOB are both equilateral triangles. Thus ∠AOB = 60°, ∠OBC = 60°, and therefore OA is parallel to BC. Triangle ABC and triangle OBC have BC as the same base, and A and O are on the line OA parallel to BC, so their heights are equal and their areas are equal. The shaded area can be regarded as triangle ABC plus the circular segment between chord BC and minor arc BC; after replacing triangle ABC with triangle OBC of equal area, the shaded area is equal to the area of sector OBC. The radius is 2 cm and the central angle is 60°, so the sector area is (60/360) × π × 2² = 2π/3.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a circle centered at O with regular hexagon A-B-C-D-E-F inscribed, and the shaded region bounded by side AB, diagonal AC, and the minor arc BC. From the text, use radius 2 cm and that the hexagon is regular. Draw OB, OC, and OA. In a regular inscribed hexagon, adjacent central angles are 60 degrees and each side equals the radius, so triangles OBC and AOB are equilateral. Hence OA is parallel to BC, making triangles ABC and OBC have the same base BC and the same height. The shaded region is triangle ABC plus the circular segment between chord BC and arc BC; replacing triangle ABC by equal-area triangle OBC gives exactly sector OBC. From the text, use that the circle radius is 2 cm and the inscribed hexagon is regular. Since an inscribed regular hexagon has side length equal to the radius, AB = BC = 2. $\therefore OA \parallel BC$,\\

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle with O as the center, and a regular hexagon is inscribed in the circle, with vertices labeled in order as A, B, C, D, E, F. The shaded part is located at the lower left of the circle, enclosed by side AB, diagonal AC, and the lower small arc corresponding to BC; the center O is inside the hexagon. Reasoning: Connect OB, OC, OA. A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle, so the central angle corresponding to adjacent vertices is 60°, and the side length equals the radius, so triangle OBC and triangle AOB are both equilateral triangles. Thus ∠AOB = 60°, ∠OBC = 60°, and therefore OA is parallel to BC. Triangle ABC and triangle OBC have BC as the same base, and A and O are on the line OA parallel to BC, so their heights are equal and their areas are equal. The shaded area can be regarded as triangle ABC plus the circular segment between chord BC and minor arc BC; after replacing triangle ABC with triangle OBC of equal area, the shaded area is equal to the area of sector OBC. The radius is 2 cm and the central angle is 60°, so the sector area is (60/360) × π × 2² = 2π/3.
